meta.title: The Wrong Size
meta.textType: story: a shopping talk with a clear place

paragraphs: On Sunday, December sixth, at eleven o'clock, Tom and Ben went to a sports store. Tom's old football boots were too small for his feet. He saved his pocket money for two months, so he wanted new boots. The store sold balls, shirts, trainers, and boots. Ben picked up a ball and held it under his arm. Tom put his old boots on a bench. A shop assistant came to them. "Whose boots are these?" he asked. "They are mine, and they are too small now," said Tom.

Tom pointed at a pair of black leather boots on a shelf. "Do you have these boots in size forty-three?" he asked. "Yes, I will bring a box," said the assistant. He came back with a shoe box and a smile. Tom sat down and tried on the boots. First he put one boot on his foot, and then the other. He stood up, walked two steps, and stopped. "They are too tight," he said. "My toes touch the front." "Let me bring the next size, forty-four," said the assistant. Tom tried on the new boots, and this time he smiled. "They are just right," said Tom.

Ben looked at the tag on the box. The old price was one thousand baht. The new price was eight hundred baht. A red sign on the shelf said "SALE", so the boots were cheaper. "Is eight hundred baht too much?" asked Ben. "No, because I saved my money for two months," said Tom. "I do not want to spend more today."

The boys went to the desk, and Tom paid. Another customer waited behind them. The assistant gave Tom a receipt. Tom put the receipt in his pocket and took the box under his arm. Ben put the ball back on its shelf and bought a pair of white socks. "Thank you," said the assistant to both boys.
At the door, Ben looked at the box. "Boots are expensive, but they are good boots," he said. "I know, and I will take care of them," said Tom. Ben laughed, and they walked out into the warm street.

sentences.text: On Sunday, December sixth, at eleven o'clock, Tom and Ben went to a sports store.
Tom's old football boots were too small for his feet.
He saved his pocket money for two months, so he wanted new boots.
The store sold balls, shirts, trainers, and boots.
Ben picked up a ball and held it under his arm.
Tom put his old boots on a bench.
A shop assistant came to them.
"Whose boots are these?" he asked.
"They are mine, and they are too small now," said Tom.
Tom pointed at a pair of black leather boots on a shelf.
"Do you have these boots in size forty-three?" he asked.
"Yes, I will bring a box," said the assistant.
He came back with a shoe box and a smile.
Tom sat down and tried on the boots.
First he put one boot on his foot, and then the other.
He stood up, walked two steps, and stopped.
"They are too tight," he said.
"My toes touch the front."
"Let me bring the next size, forty-four," said the assistant.
Tom tried on the new boots, and this time he smiled.
"They are just right," said Tom.
Ben looked at the tag on the box.
The old price was one thousand baht.
The new price was eight hundred baht.
A red sign on the shelf said "SALE", so the boots were cheaper.
"Is eight hundred baht too much?" asked Ben.
"No, because I saved my money for two months," said Tom.
"I do not want to spend more today."
The boys went to the desk, and Tom paid.
Another customer waited behind them.
The assistant gave Tom a receipt.
Tom put the receipt in his pocket and took the box under his arm.
Ben put the ball back on its shelf and bought a pair of white socks.
"Thank you," said the assistant to both boys.
At the door, Ben looked at the box.
"Boots are expensive, but they are good boots," he said.
"I know, and I will take care of them," said Tom.
Ben laughed, and they walked out into the warm street.
